stories.title: Hijack threat note found in Air India lavatory
stories.summary: A hijack threat found in a lavatory forced an Air India flight to abort take-off in Kolkata. The note claimed the flight would be hijacked at 11:11. The aircraft, carrying 105 passengers, was screened again before departing seven hours late. The note did not specify a date.

stories.title: Maharashtra CM opposes shifting international flights to Navi Mumbai
stories.summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has opposed plans to relocate 14 international flight routes from Mumbai to the new Navi Mumbai airport. He suggested a phased redevelopment of Terminal 1 instead, proposing the construction of a new Terminal 1B to maintain capacity while the existing facility is rebuilt.

stories.title: IndiGo and Air India diverge on international growth
stories.summary: IndiGo and Air India are pursuing different international expansion strategies. IndiGo is focusing on long-haul growth built upon its existing narrow-body operations, while Air India is attempting to improve the financial performance of its current network and recover traffic previously lost to foreign carriers.

stories.title: Air India loss reduction aids Singapore Airlines
stories.summary: Singapore Airlines reported a 44 percent decline in first-half net profit to SGD 134 million. The group's results were partially offset by a reduction in losses at Air India, where it holds a 25.1 percent stake. The Indian carrier's losses narrowed by approximately 2,000 crore rupees.

stories.title: Most Mumbai international traffic to stay at Terminal 2
stories.summary: Around 91 percent of international passenger traffic at Mumbai airport will remain unaffected during the redevelopment of Terminal 1. Sources indicate 39 of 50 international airlines will continue operations from Terminal 2. About 5 million passengers are expected to move to the new Navi Mumbai airport.

stories.title: Air India losses narrow by 2,000 crore rupees
stories.summary: Singapore Airlines reported a 43.9 percent decline in first-half net profit. The group's share of losses from its 25.1 percent stake in Air India narrowed by 510 crore rupees. Total losses for the Tata Group-owned airline are estimated at 10,837 crore rupees for the period.

stories.title: Fadnavis proposes phased Mumbai airport redevelopment
stories.summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has proposed a phased redevelopment plan for Mumbai airport's Terminal 1. The strategy involves building a new Terminal 1B before demolishing and reconstructing Terminal 1A. The plan aims to address structural and safety concerns while maintaining continuous flight operations for passengers.

stories.title: Fadnavis denies flight relocation to Navi Mumbai
stories.summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has opposed the proposed shifting of international flights from Mumbai to the new Navi Mumbai airport. The Chief Minister's Office stated there is no current proposal to transfer flights, despite earlier reports regarding the relocation of services for the summer season.

stories.title: IndiGo extends Saudi Arabia flight suspension
stories.summary: IndiGo has extended the suspension of flights to four Saudi Arabian cities, citing regional security considerations. Services to Jeddah and Madinah are suspended until November 21, while flights to Riyadh and Dammam are cancelled through November 30. The airline is offering refunds or re-accommodation to affected passengers.

stories.title: India international passenger traffic hits 78.7 million
stories.summary: India's international air passenger traffic rose 6 percent to 78.7 million in the year ended March 2026. The share of Indian carriers in this traffic declined to 44.4 percent. Total air passenger traffic increased 2.7 percent to 246.1 million, according to official civil aviation statistics.

stories.title: Dispute over Mumbai flight redistribution continues
stories.summary: Adani Airport Holdings has proposed shifting flights to 14 international destinations to the new Navi Mumbai airport to accommodate Terminal 1 redevelopment. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has intervened to oppose the move. The airport operator says it cannot accommodate all requested flights for summer 2027.

stories.title: Air India shortlists executive for CFO role
stories.summary: Air India has shortlisted Balagopal Kunduvara for the position of chief financial officer. Kunduvara, a former Singapore Airlines executive, recently left his role as finance chief at Garuda Indonesia. The appointment is part of the airline's effort to strengthen financial management amid ongoing cost-reduction exercises.

stories.title: easyJet shareholders approve Apollo takeover
stories.summary: easyJet shareholders have approved a 5.7 billion pound takeover by private equity firm Apollo. The deal is expected to close by the end of March 2027, subject to regulatory approval. Completion will end the airline's 25-year listing on the London Stock Exchange.

stories.title: United Airlines restricts AI booking agents
stories.summary: United Airlines has restricted the use of AI agents for booking flights on its platform and through third-party aggregators. The carrier cited potential violations of Department of Transportation and FAA regulations, noting that AI agents could expose sensitive passenger information and lead to unintended account changes.

stories.title: United Airlines blocks AI booking agents
stories.summary: United Airlines is restricting AI agents from booking flights through its website and third-party agencies. The airline stated that AI poses security and privacy risks, including the potential for unauthorized account changes. United joins other businesses in blocking these agents to protect user credentials and payment details.

stories.title: United loyalty program ranks second globally
stories.summary: United Airlines MileagePlus has moved up three spots to become the second-ranked airline loyalty program globally, according to Point.me. Air France-KLM Flying Blue maintained the top spot for the third consecutive year. Only three U.S. airlines appeared in the top 10 rankings for 2026.

stories.title: Shareholders back 5.7 billion pound easyJet buyout
stories.summary: easyJet shareholders have voted to back a 5.7 billion pound takeover by Apollo. The deal will take the airline private, ending 26 years of public trading. Apollo will hold up to 49.9 percent of the company, with the remainder held by rollover shareholders and the EU Trust.

stories.title: United CEO calls for more O'Hare staff
stories.summary: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby has urged the FAA to increase staffing at Chicago O'Hare's south control tower. Kirby claimed that current shortages are the primary cause of long taxi times, suggesting that proper staffing levels could reduce wait times by six or seven minutes for passengers.

stories.title: TUI surveys holiday habits
stories.summary: TUI surveyed 2,000 people to predict 2027 travel, proposing a year of multiple short trips instead of one annual holiday. The study introduces a concept the company calls Hushpitality. The outlook arrived alongside news of job cuts and repair delays across the airline's operations.

stories.title: Two European carriers halt operations
stories.summary: Slovakia's AirExplore and Spain's AlbaStar stopped flying on November 10, citing difficult macroeconomic conditions. AlbaStar described the situation as temporary while it discusses options with potential investors. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Singapore Airlines returns to profit
stories.summary: Singapore Airlines reported a return to profitability for the first half of fiscal 2026-27, citing double-digit growth in passenger and cargo yields. Higher operating costs followed the onset of the Middle East conflict, and the airline's investment in Air India continues to weigh on results. The full piece is for

stories.title: Dan Air enters insolvency
stories.summary: Romanian budget airline Dan Air officially entered insolvency on November 6. The carrier, which launched commercial flights in 2023, saw its debt grow from 19 million USD in 2024 to 26.5 million USD in 2025. The airline is currently not providing refunds to passengers.

stories.title: United CEO compares O'Hare taxi times to road trips
stories.summary: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby blamed FAA understaffing for long taxi times at Chicago O'Hare, suggesting that full staffing could save several minutes. Kirby likened the wait to driving to Milwaukee, a city 79 miles away. The airport remains known for its long taxiing.

stories.title: Cathay Group expands Airbus order
stories.summary: Cathay Group ordered 14 additional Airbus aircraft, including 11 A330-900s and three A321neos. The deal is part of a fleet renewal program with a commitment exceeding 19.2 billion USD through 2035. The order brings the group's total firm commitment for the A330-900 to 41 jets.

stories.title: Boeing 737 MAX 10 order book
stories.summary: Boeing's 737 MAX 10 received FAA type certification on October 20, 2026. The manufacturer reports that more than 30 customers have placed firm orders for 1,555 aircraft. Several major airlines have committed to the largest member of the 737 MAX family, with orders ranging from 100 to 167 jets.

stories.title: CDB Aviation leases jets to Freebird Airlines
stories.summary: CDB Aviation has leased two Airbus A321ceo aircraft to Turkish carrier Freebird Airlines. The jets will feature a special livery to mark the airline's 25th anniversary. The transaction supports the continued development of the carrier's all-Airbus fleet.

stories.title: Emirates buys back leased A380s
stories.summary: Emirates has agreed to purchase six Airbus A380s currently leased from Qatar's Lesha Bank. The airline has already taken ownership of two aircraft, with the remaining four to follow by April 2028. The airline expects the jets to remain in service for up to 25 years.

stories.title: Cathay orders 11 Airbus A330-900s and three A321neos
stories.summary: Hong Kong’s Cathay Group has placed a firm order for 14 additional Airbus aircraft. Airbus announced the deal on 11 November 2026, it comprises 11 widebody A330-900s and three single-aisle A321neos. The order brings Cathay’s firm commitments for the A330-900 to 41 aircraft, following an

stories.title: Embraer reports record revenue
stories.summary: Embraer raised its 2026 guidance after reporting third-quarter revenue of 2.35 billion USD, an increase of 17% over the previous year. The manufacturer recorded no US import tariffs in its executive and support units during the quarter, compared to 17 million USD in tariffs a year earlier.

stories.title: Comac tests smaller C919 derivative
stories.summary: Chinese manufacturer Comac has begun flight testing a shortened version of its C919 narrowbody jet. While many competitors focus on stretching aircraft to increase capacity, Comac is targeting high-altitude airports with this smaller derivative. The choice deviates from current trends in the narrowbody market.

stories.title: Magnifica Air revealed as A220 buyer
stories.summary: US startup Magnifica Air is the customer behind an order for 10 Airbus A220-300 jets. The company intends to configure the aircraft for 54 passengers, offering amenities typically found in private aviation. The order was previously listed under an unidentified customer in the manufacturer's backlog.

stories.title: Boeing deliveries fall in October
stories.summary: Boeing delivered 49 aircraft in October, a 14% decline from September and lower than the 53 delivered in October 2025. The manufacturer continues to face production challenges. Despite the delivery drop, Boeing recorded its strongest October for new orders, according to company reports.

stories.title: Cathay Pacific orders 11 Airbus aircraft with $5.1 bn list price
stories.summary: Cathay Pacific has ordered 11 more Airbus jets with a list price of $5.1 billion, the Hong Kong airline said Wednesday. The 11 A330-900 jets "will support the growth of Cathay Pacific's regional network and provide it with more passenger and cargo capacity", the company

stories.title: FAA expands SMART AI tool to 22 US air traffic centers
stories.summary: The FAA has expanded its SMART air traffic planning tool to all 22 US en-route control centers. The agency says the system helped reroute 180 flights in the Washington area, saving fuel and time. The system was introduced in September 2026 for limited use near Washington.

stories.title: United Airlines bans AI agents from booking flights
stories.summary: United Airlines is banning AI agents from booking flights for travelers, citing security risks and potential federal rule violations. The airline says sharing account credentials with third-party software is a problem. Many consumers currently use AI tools to track deals and make purchases.

stories.title: Five federal agencies agree to coordinate counter-drone technology
stories.summary: Five federal departments have signed a memorandum of understanding to coordinate the testing and deployment of counter-drone technologies. The agreement aims to address unauthorized drone threats without disrupting civilian aviation. The FAA and FCC will assist as agencies develop systems to detect and control unauthorized drones.

stories.title: Midwest flights grounded after Minnesota air traffic facility outage
stories.summary: Flights in Minnesota and nine other Midwest states were diverted or held on the ground Thursday due to a system outage at a Minneapolis air traffic control facility. Radar and ATC systems have since returned to service. The facility handles traffic across 330,000 square miles.

stories.title: UK air traffic control apologizes for outages
stories.summary: UK air traffic control has issued an apology following recent system outages. The organization confirmed that the technical issues have been resolved. Further details regarding the cause of the disruption were not provided in the available report.

stories.title: FAA proposes airworthiness directive for Diamond DA50 C
stories.summary: The FAA is proposing an airworthiness directive for Diamond DA 50 C aircraft following reports of flap actuator failures. Investigations found that a failed actuator could interfere with aileron control. The agency says the condition could limit a pilot's ability to control the aircraft.

stories.title: NTSB and FAA continue investigation into deadly plane crash
stories.summary: The NTSB and FAA are continuing their investigation into a deadly plane crash. No further details regarding the incident or the findings of the investigation were provided in the available text.

stories.title: Delhi High Court rejects plea for airline conduct rules
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has rejected a petition seeking specific rules to address misconduct by airline staff toward passengers. Justice Amit Mahajan stated that the court cannot compel the government to formulate regulations, noting that such policy matters fall within the domain of competent authorities.

stories.title: FAA investigates near-miss at LAX
stories.summary: The FAA is investigating an incident where an Air France Airbus A350 turned into the path of an American Airlines Airbus A321 shortly after takeoff from LAX. A controller warned the American pilots that the other aircraft was less than a mile ahead. Both flights landed safely.

stories.title: FAA authorizes long-range drone operations over Gulf of Mexico
stories.summary: The FAA has authorized a drone to fly beyond the operator's visual line of sight over the Gulf of Mexico. The agency says the move marks a milestone in advancing American drone dominance and aviation innovation. The authorization allows for commercial drone operations over the high seas.

stories.title: Two planes nearly collide at LAX
stories.summary: The FAA reported that two planes nearly collided at Los Angeles International Airport. No further details regarding the specific aircraft involved or the circumstances of the incident were provided in the available text.

stories.title: Two class-action lawsuits allege US airline price coordination
stories.summary: Two new class-action lawsuits have been filed alleging that US airlines are coordinating prices. The full details of the allegations and the status of the legal proceedings are available to subscribers of the source publication.

stories.title: Number of women pilots in UK rising twice as fast as men
stories.summary: The number of pilot licenses held by women in the UK is growing at twice the rate of those held by men, according to the Civil Aviation Authority. Women held 1,218 commercial licenses as of October 2026, a 5.4 percent increase since the start of the year.

stories.title: United Airlines captain Carole Hopson to speak at Purdue
stories.summary: United Airlines Boeing 737 captain Carole Hopson will speak at Purdue University on November 19. Hopson, a former journalist and executive, will discuss her career change to aviation. The event is part of the Purdue Polytechnic Aviation Lecture Series and is open to the public.

stories.title: WASP pilot Nadine Ramsey inducted into Kansas Aviation Hall of Fame
stories.summary: Nadine Ramsey, one of 26 Women Airforce Service Pilots to fly the P-38 Lightning during World War II, was posthumously inducted into the Kansas Aviation Hall of Fame. Ramsey was one of the first women to fly mail for the postal service.

stories.title: Data shows rising share of women pilots
stories.summary: The number of women holding pilot licenses in the UK and US is increasing, though women still represent less than 7 percent of commercial license holders in the UK. Industry leaders say significant work is needed to address structural barriers and disproportionate scrutiny in the field.

stories.title: Joramco Academy welcomes new intake of students
stories.summary: Joramco Academy has welcomed its new intake of students for the 2026 academic year. The program consists of two years of theoretical learning followed by two years of practical experience. The academy also maintains a joint bachelor's program in aeronautical engineering with the University of Jordan.

stories.title: AFGSC expands B-1 pilot training
stories.summary: The Air Force Global Strike Command has launched a new aviation initiative to expand B-1 pilot training. Further details regarding the scope and implementation of the initiative are not available in the provided text.

stories.title: Simorg software to manage AeronautX training centre
stories.summary: Turkish software provider Gözen Digital Aviation is partnering with AeronautX to integrate its Simorg platform into a new Amsterdam pilot training facility. The system will handle bookings, scheduling, and student progress. The software is designed to provide a centralised digital system for managing the new training centre operations.

stories.title: Sevenair Academy hosts second group of ANA cadets
stories.summary: Sevenair Academy has welcomed its second group of 11 All Nippon Airways cadets to its campus in Portugal. The training is part of the Airbus ATPi Cadet Program. The academy currently reports approximately 250 cadets in training and operates a fleet of 44 aircraft for its students.

stories.title: US Air Force uses HondaJet for B-1B pilot training
stories.summary: The US Air Force has launched the Bomber Supplemental Trainer for Aircrew Readiness program to increase flight hours for B-1B Lancer pilots. Using contractor-operated HondaJet aircraft, the initiative aims to save airframe hours for demanding missions. The first training sortie took place on 2 November in Texas.

stories.title: FlyBy Aviation Academy adds Tecnam aircraft to fleet
stories.summary: FlyBy Aviation Academy has added a new Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft to its training fleet in Spain. This expansion brings the academy to 47 total aircraft. The school provides professional pilot training to an international student population representing more than 115 nationalities across its two training facilities.

stories.title: Ryan Aerospace debuts mixed reality T-6 trainer
stories.summary: Australian manufacturer Ryan Aerospace has introduced a T-6 Texan II training device that combines a physical cockpit with a Varjo XR-4 mixed reality headset. The system allows students to use physical controls in a simulated environment. It will be displayed at the I/ITSEC conference in late November.

stories.title: Cape Fear Community College moves aviation program
stories.summary: Cape Fear Community College has relocated its aviation maintenance technician program to a new 3,700-square-foot facility at Wilmington International Airport. The program previously shared space with diesel technician students at the college North Campus. The instructor noted they are still moving equipment to find the most efficient layout.

research.title: A Beltrami Mode in Extreme Fractional Hydrodynamics under Stochastic Forcing
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an exact stochastic solution of the extreme order endpoint of adaptive fractional Navier Stokes (AFNS) hydrodynamics on the three-dimensional periodic torus. A helical Beltrami eigenfield reduces the nonlinear vector equation to a scalar Ornstein. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Aeroelastically Constrained Optimal Path Planning of a Fixed-Wing Airborne Wind Energy System
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-megawatt fixed-wing airborne wind energy systems (AWES) use an aircraft with large, slender wings that deform over the pumping cycle. To harvest maximum energy, the cycle is usually designed by means of dedicated reference trajectory optimization. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: An Accurate Modulation-Assisted Method for Phasor Estimation Under Decaying DC Offsets
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Decaying DC (DDC) offsets severely compromise the accurate estimation of current phasors immediately following power grid fault occurrence. Consequently, conventional full-cycle discrete Fourier transform (FCDFT) algorithms experience decaying oscillatory magnitude errors, potentially causing distance relays to. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: An Idealized Model of Buoyant Gas Spreading and Silt Release beneath Rough Cave Ceilings
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gas exhaled by open-circuit divers collects under the ceilings of submerged caves, migrates along the rock, and dislodges loose silt that then falls through the passage, a process that cave divers call percolation. This study develops. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Banding instabilities in poroelastic media under flow-driven compaction
research.summary: Announce Type: cross Abstract: When cross-linked poroelastic media are subjected to a hydrostatic pressure difference, they compact, remaining fully swollen on their uppermost surface and becoming increasingly compressed with depth. A critical unexplored effect of cross-linking and resistance to shear. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
